subject: Request: Promotional allowance review and potential top-up for MicroCo AI
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@microco.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Request: promotional allowance review and potential top-up

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the quick onboarding — MicroCo AI is live with a narrow internal beta. We hit the standard self-serve promo limit unusually fast due to heavy eval traffic from our ML team. We believe the usage is legitimate: multiple researchers running long-context tests and embeddings.

Can Redwood approve a one-time top-up (50k tokens) or extend our trial window by 7 days while we finalize our procurement? We can provide signup logs and a PO if helpful. We’re trying to move quickly on a pilot that could expand to a paid commitment.

Attached: microco-usage.csv (summary export).

Appreciate any fast path here — happy to hop on a 15-min call.

Best,
Elena Soto
Head of Ops
MicroCo AI
[phone redacted]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@microco.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: promotional allowance review and potential top-up

Thanks Elena — congrats on the beta launch. I’ve looped in Marissa from Risk and Neha from Sales Ops to help validate the request.

Quick asks to triage:
- Can you confirm whether the signups come from corporate email addresses or personal/disposable domains?
- Any shared test accounts or CI runners that might have pumped traffic?
- Approximate number of unique users running long-context runs vs automated jobs.

We’ll review the usage file you attached and get back with either a quick top-up or ask for more evidence. If things look green we can push a 25k token top-up immediately while procurement completes.

Attaching your CSV to the case.

— Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: microco-usage.csv]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 13:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: promotional allowance review and potential top-up

Sergio / Neha — I pulled the usage and did a quick signal pass. High level: some legitimate activity but several concerning indicators that warrant holding a full top-up.

Findings (summary):
- 72% of heavy token runs originate from 18 accounts created in the last 72 hours. Several use gmail/dmarc-free disposable domains (list attached).
- Device fingerprints show a very narrow entropy: same browser UA strings varying only by minor build numbers, identical viewport sizes, and repeated connection IP blocks across sessions.
- Rapid repeated token bursts that align more with automated stress tests than manual exploration.

Attachments: suspicious-signups.csv (account list + signals), device-heatmap.png (cluster map).

Recommended path:
1) Hold full 50k token grant.
2) Offer a provisional 10–25k token manual top-up under monitoring and with automatic rollback if bot signals increase.
3) Ask MicroCo for signup logs (auth timestamps, IPs, device IDs) and a PO from procurement to expedite a permanent allocation.

I can lead the investigation if you want me on the call with MicroCo.

—Marissa
Risk & Trust Manager, Redwood Inference

[Attachments: suspicious-signups.csv, device-heatmap.png]

From: Elena Soto <elena@microco.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Jake Lin <jake@microco.ai>, procurements@microco.ai
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: promotional allowance review and potential top-up

Marissa — thanks for the quick checks. A few notes from our side:
- All prod/test accounts are managed from our corporate SSO; I’ll export the signup logs but there are also lab accounts created by contractors that might have used personal emails. We flagged those for cleanup last week.
- The heavy runs are from two internal experiment queues (names: bert-long-eval, embedding-bench) — engineers intentionally run long sessions for model comparisons.
- I’m attaching the signup log PDF and a preliminary PO (po_3489.pdf) to show intent to purchase.

We’re happy to accept a provisional smaller top-up plus monitoring. If it helps speed things, approve 20k now and we’ll share the full logs by EOD.

Best,
Elena
[Attachment: microco-signup-log.pdf]
[Attachment: po_3489.pdf]

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: promotional allowance review and potential top-up

Thanks for the thread. I reviewed Marissa’s signals and Elena’s docs quickly. Given the PO and the customer willingness to share logs, I’m comfortable approving a constrained provisional top-up.

Decision:
- Approve a 20,000-token manual top-up to MicroCo AI (MC-2027-042) immediately.
- Implement a 48-hour enhanced monitoring window with automatic rollback to 0 tokens for the top-up if bot-score > 0.7 for more than 3 distinct accounts.
- Require procurement/PO or SSO-confirmed corporate domains within 72 hours to convert to a permanent allocation.

Sergio — please issue the top-up and enable the monitoring policy on the account. If Marissa’s team needs raw logs for deeper analysis, grant them access to the evidence folder.

— Dev Patel
Director, Platform Ops

[Note: actioned in platform — provisional top-up queued]
